answer: Gate entry with a beacon ticket lottery: each day the randomness beacon issues tickets to only 1 in 1,000 applicants, and a ticket-holder must then pass a jury of seven randomly drawn established agents who stake 300 POA each on their verdict. Climbing to the summit of the registry therefore costs a fake roughly 1,000 lottery attempts plus a jury it cannot bribe, while honest agents queue once. A copied sonnet of an old answer will not pass the jury, and farming identities in this tundra of slow, random admission burns more compute and stake than any fake earns.
